issues.legal_issue: A testamentary direction permitting sale of property while giving beneficiaries an option to partition requires the executor to consent to partition when the beneficiaries exercise that option before conveyance.
material_facts: The will authorized the executor to sell the property and distribute the proceeds, but also allowed the beneficiaries to partition the property into four lots, with the executor to consent if they chose that course.
The will provided that each beneficiary would inherit the allotted property absolutely after partition.
issues.conclusion: The executor was required to consent to partition if the beneficiaries expressed that desire before a deed of sale was executed. An executor generally has power to transfer the testator’s property, but the effect of that power on the agreement in this case was not necessary to decide.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 211(1) and 307(1) of the Indian Succession Act, 1925 give an executor power to transfer the testator’s property, as recognized in Smt. Babuain Chandrakala Devi v. Smt. Pokhraj Kuer and P.H. Alphonso v. Mrs. Irene Dias. The will’s terms nevertheless gave the beneficiaries an option to partition, which the executor had to respect if exercised before sale.

predicates.testamentary_property_dispute: The dispute concerns property governed by a testamentary instrument.
predicates.will_authorizes_sale_and_grants_partitio: The will authorizes the executor to sell the property but also gives beneficiaries an option to partition it.
predicates.beneficiaries_request_partition_before_c: The beneficiaries express a desire to partition the property before a deed of sale is executed.

issues.definition: When a dispute concerns a will that authorizes sale but grants beneficiaries a partition option, and they request partition before conveyance, the executor must consent to partition.

issues.legal_issue: An agreement expressly subject to ratification by persons who are not parties does not become a concluded contract until ratification is obtained.
material_facts: The agreement provided that the executor agreed to convey the property for himself and as executor, subject to ratification by the co-heirs.
The purchaser drafted the agreement, and the executor made corrections to it.
The draft sale deeds contemplated conveyance by the other beneficiaries, represented by the executor under powers of attorney.
The purchaser had advised the executor to obtain powers of attorney from the other beneficiaries, and ratification was not obtained.
issues.conclusion: The agreement was conditional rather than a concluded contract and could not be specifically enforced.
issues.legal_principle: A clause making an agreement subject to ratification by non-parties is a condition precedent to a concluded contract. The court relied on Henry Earnest Meaney v. E.C. Eyre Walker, which discussed the requirement of an absolute and unqualified acceptance under section 7 of the Contract Act, and Warehousing & Forwarding Company of East Africa Ltd. v. Jafferali & Sons Ltd., which held that where the other contracting party knows ratification is required, neither party is bound until ratification is duly communicated. Dr. Jiwan Lal v. Brij Mohan Mehra was distinguished because the relevant condition there was for the purchaser’s benefit and could be waived; the ratification condition here was not for the purchaser’s benefit.

predicates.specific_performance_proceeding: A party seeks specific performance of an agreement to convey property.
predicates.agreement_expressly_requires_ratificatio: The agreement states that it is subject to approval or ratification by persons who are not parties to it.
predicates.ratification_not_obtained: The required persons have not ratified the agreement.

issues.definition: If specific performance is sought and an agreement requires ratification by non-parties that has not been obtained, the agreement is not concluded or specifically enforceable.

issues.legal_issue: Specific performance may be refused when the circumstances and subsequent events make its exercise inequitable.
material_facts: The purchaser was both a tenant of part of the property and a practicing advocate who had advised the executor about the property and a possible sale.

The purchaser's correspondence raised the prospect that the Rent Controller could allot vacant premises to another person, and the court found that he created a scare about that possibility while negotiating to buy the property.
The purchaser drafted the agreement and had an upper hand in the negotiations.
The beneficiaries later obtained a partition decree under which the house was allotted to them according to their shares.
The purchasers had paid nothing to the beneficiaries, and the purchaser did not challenge the partition decree in later proceedings concerning his tenancy.
issues.conclusion: In any event, the circumstances and subsequent events made this an unfit case for exercising the discretionary jurisdiction to grant specific performance.
issues.legal_principle: Section 20 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963 confers discretionary jurisdiction over specific performance. The court relied on V. Muthusami (Dead) by Lrs. v. Angammal and Nirmala Anand v. Advent Corporation (P) Ltd. in declining to exercise that discretion in light of the purchaser’s conduct and subsequent events.

predicates.specific_performance_appeal: An appeal concerns a claim for specific performance of an agreement to convey property.
predicates.purchaser_used_advisory_or_tenant_positi: The purchaser used a position as a tenant, adviser, or both to gain an advantage in negotiations for the property.
predicates.subsequent_partition_decree_allotted_pro: A later partition decree allotted the property to other beneficiaries according to their shares.
predicates.purchaser_paid_no_consideration: The purchaser paid no consideration to the persons to whom the property was later allotted.

issues.definition: In an appeal concerning specific performance, when the purchaser used a tenant or advisory position to gain an advantage, a later partition decree allotted the property to others, and the purchaser paid no consideration, discretionary specific-performance relief is denied.
